mainTopic: The severance gift (הענקה), which heirs a Hebrew slave serves, and the inheritance rights of a נכרי and a גר
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of which items are left out of the הענקה, the gift given to a freed עבד עברי. A ברייתא then brings two views. The תנא קמא says the gift is always given, sized by how much the master was blessed. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says it is given only if the house was blessed because of the slave, and that the doubled verb is just ordinary speech. Next, a ברייתא lists who keeps serving the master's children after he dies. A regular עבד עברי serves the son but not the daughter, while an אמה עבריה, a נרצע, and one sold to a נכרי serve no heir. The גמרא finds a פסוק for each rule and explains why the son, not the brother, takes the father's place. From חזקיה's פסוק, רבא learns that a נכרי inherits his father by Torah law, while a גר inherits his non-Jewish father only מדרבנן, and proves this from a משנה about idols. Finally, nobody inherits a גר, not even מדרבנן. The גמרא starts to resolve a contradiction about repaying a גר's sons, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What each opinion excludes from the gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that, according to one master (רבי שמעון), the extra word in the פסוק comes to exclude money, and according to the other (רבי אליעזר), it comes to exclude mules.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to one Master, it comes to exclude money. According to the other Master, it comes to exclude mules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier question. Each opinion uses the extra word in the פסוק to leave out a different item from the הענקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי שמעון and רבי אליעזר each built a rule about what kind of items go into the gift. The גמרא now shows that each of them still has a use for the remaining word of the פסוק: רבי שמעון uses it to leave out money, and רבי אליעזר uses it to leave out mules.

keyTerms.meaning: According to one Master (one of the two opinions)
To exclude, to leave out
Money
Mules

phrases.english: According to one Master — to exclude money,
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון, from just before this part of the daf.

phrases.english: according to the other Master — to exclude mules.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָר – לְמַעוֹטֵי כְּסָפִים, לְמָר – לְמַעוֹטֵי פְּרָדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question from just before this part of the daf about how each opinion uses the remaining word of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each opinion uses the word to exclude something different: money for one, mules for the other.

steps.title: The gift is given in every case
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא considers making the gift depend on whether the house was blessed because of the slave. It rejects this idea, because the doubled verb 'העניק תעניק' teaches that the gift is given in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'With which ה׳ your God has blessed you.' One might think that if the house was blessed because of him, we give him a gift, and if not, we do not. So the verse says 'העניק תעניק', meaning in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא raises a possible reading of 'אשר ברכך' and then rejects it. The doubled verb shows that the master must always give the gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אשר ברכך' could suggest that the gift depends on the slave bringing blessing. The ברייתא answers that the doubled form 'העניק תעניק' makes the gift a duty no matter what happened.

keyTerms.meaning: The severance gift a master gives a released Hebrew slave
The house was blessed because of him
'One might think' (the opening of a reading that will be rejected)
The verse teaches, the verse says
In any case

steps.confusionAlert: The 'יכול' part is not the ברייתא's ruling. It is a reading the ברייתא raises only so it can reject it.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"With which the Lord your God has blessed you."
phrases.notes: דברים 15:14

phrases.english: One might think: if the house was blessed because of him —
we give him a severance gift,
if the house was not blessed because of him —
we do not give him a severance gift.
Therefore the verse says: "You shall surely give him severance" —
in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about the conditions for giving the gift.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The master must give the severance gift whether or not the house was blessed because of the slave.

steps.title: Then why say 'with which He blessed you'?
steps.stepSummary: Since the gift is given in every case, the ברייתא asks what the words 'אשר ברכך' come to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the verse teach by saying 'with which He has blessed you'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a follow-up question. If the gift does not depend on blessing, the words 'אשר ברכך' seem to have no job. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word of the Torah needs a purpose. The ruling in the last step took away the obvious meaning of 'אשר ברכך', so the ברייתא must find it a new role.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
What does the verse come to teach?

phrases.english: If so,
what does the verse teach by saying "with which He has blessed you"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אֲשֶׁר בֵּרַכְךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the phrase 'אשר ברכך' is for, now that step 2 says the gift does not depend on blessing.

steps.title: The size of the gift follows the blessing
steps.stepSummary: The words 'אשר ברכך' teach how big the gift should be: the master gives according to how much he has been blessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Give him everything according to the blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. 'אשר ברכך' tells us how much to give, not whether to give.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, the duty to give comes from 'העניק תעניק'. The amount comes from 'אשר ברכך': a master with more wealth gives a bigger gift.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the blessing (how much one has)
Give him

steps.whatToRemember: According to the תנא קמא, the gift is always given. 'העניק תעניק' creates the duty, and 'אשר ברכך' sets the size.

phrases.english: Give him everything according to the blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אשר ברכך' sets the size of the gift according to the master's wealth.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: the gift depends on blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה reads the פסוק simply: the gift is given only if the house was blessed because of the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: the words mean what they say. If the house was blessed because of him, we give him a gift. If not, we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא disagrees with the תנא קמא. It reads 'אשר ברכך' as a real condition for giving the gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, the reading the תנא קמא rejected is actually the right one. The gift depends on whether the slave brought blessing to the house.

keyTerms.meaning: The words mean what they plainly say

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
The words are as they are written.
If the house was blessed because of him — we give him a severance gift;

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִתְבָּרֵךְ בַּיִת בִּגְלָלוֹ – אֵין מַעֲנִיקִים לוֹ.
phrases.english: if the house was not blessed because of him — we do not give him a severance gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר: דְּבָרִים כִּכְתָבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gift is given only if the house was blessed because of the slave.

steps.title: Then why the doubled verb?
steps.stepSummary: If the gift depends on blessing, the ברייתא asks what the doubled verb 'העניק תעניק' comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the verse teach by saying 'העניק תעניק'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the question is turned on רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. The doubled verb was the תנא קמא's source, so what does he do with it? The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a doubled verb is read as adding a teaching. Since רבי אלעזר בן עזריה does not learn 'in any case' from it, he has to explain why the Torah doubled the word.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall surely give severance' (a doubled verb)

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying:
"You shall surely give severance"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״הַעֲנֵיק תַּעֲנִיק״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי אלעזר בן עזריה explains the doubled verb, which the תנא קמא used as his source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the doubled verb teaches according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: The Torah speaks like people speak
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה answers that the doubling is just normal human speech, so no extra teaching comes from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah spoke in the language of people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה explains that the doubled verb is simply a normal way of speaking. It does not add a new law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People often repeat a word for emphasis without meaning anything extra. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה applies this to the doubled verb here, so the plain condition of 'אשר ברכך' stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah spoke in the way people normally speak

steps.whatToRemember: The two views disagree about the doubled verb. The תנא קמא learns from it that the gift is always given. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says it is just normal speech, so the gift depends on blessing.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם' is a well-known rule of reading פסוקים, and it comes up in many places in ש"ס.

phrases.english: The Torah spoke in the language of people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled verb is ordinary human style and teaches nothing extra.

steps.title: Who keeps serving the master's heirs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that an עבד עברי serves the master's son but not his daughter. An אמה עבריה serves neither. A נרצע, and a slave sold to a non-Jew, serve neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A Hebrew slave serves the son but not the daughter. A Hebrew maidservant serves neither the son nor the daughter. A pierced slave, and one sold to a non-Jew, serve neither the son nor the daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The ברייתא lists which kinds of Hebrew slaves keep working for the master's children after the master dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sorts the slaves into groups. Only the regular עבד עברי passes to an heir, and only to a son. The others go free when the master dies.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish man sold as a slave
A Jewish girl sold as a maidservant
A slave whose ear was pierced to stay longer
A Jew who sold himself to a non-Jew

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A Hebrew slave serves the son,
phrases.notes: He means the son of the master, after the master has died.

phrases.english: but does not serve the daughter.
A Hebrew maidservant does not serve

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַבֵּן וְלֹא אֶת הַבַּת.
phrases.english: either the son or the daughter.
The pierced slave and one sold to a non-Jew

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ עוֹבֵד לֹא אֶת הַבֵּן וְלֹא אֶת הַבַּת.
phrases.english: serve neither the son nor the daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עֶבֶד עִבְרִי עוֹבֵד אֶת הַבֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: whether slaves pass to the master's heirs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a regular עבד עברי passes to an heir, and only to a son. An אמה עבריה, a נרצע, and one sold to a non-Jew pass to no heir.

steps.title: Source for serving the son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first rule of the ברייתא again and asks where we learn that an עבד עברי serves the son but not the daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: A Hebrew slave serves the son but not the daughter. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first line of the ברייתא and asks for its source. This sets up the answer, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the rule without a source. The גמרא now wants the פסוק that shows the slave passes to a son but not to a daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: The Master said:
A Hebrew slave serves the son,
but does not serve the daughter.
From where are these words derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: עֶבֶד עִבְרִי עוֹבֵד אֶת הַבֵּן, וְאֵינוֹ עוֹבֵד אֶת הַבַּת. מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the first rule of step 8 and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that an עבד עברי serves the son but not the daughter.

steps.title: The source: 'serve you' means not an heir
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'וַעֲבָדְךָ' ('he shall serve you') as limiting the slave's service to the master and not to his heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Sages taught: 'And he shall serve you six years' means you, and not an heir.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the Step 9 question by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא learns from the word 'you' that the slave does not pass to the master's heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'you' (עֲבָדְךָ) is read as a limit: the service belongs to the master personally. This is only the first half of the answer. The ברייתא still has to show that the son is an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall serve you
Heir

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"And he shall serve you six years"
phrases.notes: דברים 15:12

phrases.english: – you, and not an heir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 9 by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'you' in the verse excludes heirs from receiving the slave's service.

steps.title: Maybe the son is excluded too
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether 'you' might shut out even the son, not just other heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it means 'you and not an heir.' But maybe it means 'you and not even your son'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own reading. Perhaps the word 'you' excludes everyone, even the master's son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read on its own, the word 'you' could exclude every other person. The ברייתא needs a reason to treat the son differently from other heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: You say (opens a challenge to a reading)
Or perhaps it is only

phrases.english: You say: you and not an heir,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא: לְךָ וְלֹא לַבֵּן?
phrases.english: or perhaps it is: you and not a son?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר: לְךָ וְלֹא לַיּוֹרֵשׁ, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא: לְךָ וְלֹא לַבֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the limit learned in Step 10 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'you' exclude only distant heirs, or the son as well?

steps.title: Another verse includes the son
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים יַעֲבֹד' has no limiting word, so it includes the son. 'You' therefore excludes only other heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the other verse says 'Six years he shall labor,' the son is included. So how do I explain 'he shall serve you six years'? It means you, and not another heir.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers by bringing a second verse. That verse has no 'you' in it, so it includes the son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two verses are set side by side. One verse includes, and the other excludes. Including the son and excluding other heirs lets both verses work. That is the source for the first rule of the ברייתא in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: When it says (brings another verse)
How then do I explain
He shall labor

steps.whatToRemember: The son inherits the service of his father's עבד עברי. Other heirs do not.

phrases.english: When it says: "Six years he shall labor,"
phrases.notes: שמות 21:2

phrases.english: the son is thereby stated (included),
So how do I uphold:
"And he shall serve you six years" – you
– and not an heir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by using a second verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמות 21:2 includes the son. דברים 15:12 excludes the other heirs.

steps.title: Why the son and not the brother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the son was the one included and the brother the one left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did you see that made you include the son and leave out the brother?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא decided which relative to include. The brother could also have been the one included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses show that one relative is included and the rest are not. They do not say who that relative is. The גמרא wants a logical reason for choosing the son.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see (what is your reason)
To include
To exclude

phrases.english: What did you see to include the son,
and to exclude the brother?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַבֵּן, וּלְהוֹצִיא אֶת הָאָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the choice made in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why should the son, and not the brother, be the heir who is included?

steps.title: The son takes his father's place
steps.stepSummary: The son is included because he stands in his father's place for יעידה and for שדה אחוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include the son, because he stands in place of his father for designating the maidservant and for an ancestral field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the son already replaces his father in other areas of הלכה. So he should replace him here too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two examples. The father can do יעידה (designate an אמה עבריה as a wife) for his son. When a son redeems a field his father dedicated (שדה אחוזה), it counts as if the father redeemed it. Since the son fills his father's role in these areas, he also takes over the slave.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands in place of his father
Designating an אמה עבריה as a wife
An ancestral (inherited) field

phrases.english: I include the son –
since he stands in place of his father
for designation and for an ancestral field.
phrases.notes: The 'designation' means making the אמה עבריה a wife; the father can do this for his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 with two areas where the son replaces his father.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The son replaces his father for יעידה and for שדה אחוזה.

steps.title: But the brother replaces his brother in יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the brother should be included, since he takes his brother's place in יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! I should include the brother, since he stands in place of his brother for levirate marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא argues the other side. The brother also takes over for the dead man, through יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 used the idea of standing in someone's place. This step turns that same idea around to favor the brother. יבום is the clearest case of a relative carrying on for the one who died.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Levirate marriage: a brother marries his childless brother's widow

phrases.english: On the contrary, I include the brother
since he stands in place of his brother for levirate marriage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 14 by offering a matching reason for the brother.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning of Step 14 for preferring the son.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The brother also stands in place of the dead man, through יבום, so he has an equal claim.

steps.title: יבום only applies when there is no son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that יבום itself only happens when there is no son, so the son comes before the brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there יבום anywhere except where there is no son? If there is a son, there is no יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the brother's claim. The brother only steps in when there is no son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brother's own example works against him. The law of יבום shows that a son ranks above a brother in carrying on for the dead man. So the brother's claim cannot beat the son's.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there at all
Where there is no son

phrases.english: Is there levirate marriage
except where there is no son?
So if there is a son – there is no levirate marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ יִבּוּם אֶלָּא בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין בֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turns the challenger's own example against him.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of יבום, the brother has a claim equal to the son's.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in יבום the son comes first, so the son is the one included.

steps.title: Why was this rebuttal even needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it needed the יבום rebuttal at all. The son already has two reasons and the brother only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the only reason is this rebuttal? That suggests that without it, the brother would win! But I could learn it simply: here there are two reasons, and here only one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how the answer was built. Relying on the יבום rebuttal makes it sound like the brother would otherwise win. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son has two examples (יעידה and שדה אחוזה), and the brother has only one (יבום). Two should beat one without any further argument. So why did the גמרא need the special point about יבום?

keyTerms.meaning: A rebuttal or refutation
Is preferred
Let me derive it (from a simpler reason)
Two ... one

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not now saying the brother wins. It agrees the son is included and is only asking why the earlier argument took the longer route.

phrases.english: But is the reason only that there is this rebuttal,
so that otherwise the brother would be preferred?
Let me derive it instead
from the fact that here there are two, and here one!
phrases.notes: The 'two' are יעידה and שדה אחוזה for the son; the 'one' is יבום for the brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the way Step 16 settled the debate.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the יבום rebuttal in Step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two reasons should beat one by simple counting, so relying on the rebuttal suggests the brother would otherwise win.

steps.title: The field reason also depends on the יבום point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the שדה אחוזה reason is also built on the rule that יבום only happens when there is no son, so the יבום rebuttal was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא learns the case of the ancestral field from this same refutation as well: is there any יבום except where there is no son?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 17, which asked why the יבום rebuttal was needed. It says the field reason itself only works because of that same יבום point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 claimed the son already had two reasons, יעידה and שדה אחוזה, against the brother's one. The answer is that the son only beats the brother in שדה אחוזה because a brother steps in only when there is no son. So without the יבום point, each side really has one reason, and the rebuttal was needed after all.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation, an argument that knocks down a comparison
He derives it, he learns it out
Is there anything at all? (a rhetorical 'is there really...?')

steps.whatToRemember: The son comes before the brother because the brother's role, in יבום and in the field, only begins when there is no son.

phrases.english: An ancestral field too,

steps.title: Where do we learn that a maidservant does not serve the heirs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא, that an אמה העבריה does not serve the son or daughter, and asks for its source.

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the ברייתא and asks for its source in the Torah. It is setting up the next step, where רבי פדא answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the ברייתא said a Hebrew slave serves the son after the master dies. Here it says an אמה העבריה does not serve even the son, much less the daughter. The גמרא wants a פסוק for this difference.

steps.title: רבי פדא compares the maidservant to the pierced slave
steps.stepSummary: רבי פדא learns from 'ואף לאמתך תעשה כן' that the אמה העבריה is compared to the נרצע, who also serves no heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פדא said: the פסוק says 'And also to your maidservant you shall do likewise.' The Torah compares her to the pierced slave. Just as a pierced slave serves neither the son nor the daughter, so too a Hebrew maidservant serves neither the son nor the daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פדא gives the source. A פסוק links the maidservant to the נרצע, so she follows his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לאמתך תעשה כן' appear right after the piercing of the slave. That placement makes a היקש, a comparison between the two. A נרצע goes free when the master dies and does not serve the heirs, so the maidservant doesn't either.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah comparison that links two topics so they share rules

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי פדא. The same פסוק is already used by a ברייתא for a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually one פסוק is not used to teach two separate laws unless it has extra words. A ברייתא uses this פסוק to teach that a freed maidservant gets הענקה, just like a freed slave. So it seems the פסוק is already 'used up'.

keyTerms.meaning: To give הענקה, the parting gifts a master gives a freed Hebrew servant

steps.title: The ברייתא shows the פסוק cannot be about piercing

steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think 'do likewise' means the maidservant can also be pierced, since that topic comes right before it. But the Torah already limited piercing to 'העבד', the male slave. So the פסוק must be teaching הענקה, which makes רבי פדא's use of it look even harder.

steps.title: The extra word תעשה teaches both laws
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the extra word 'תעשה' lets the פסוק teach both הענקה and that the maidservant does not serve the heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק only had one lesson, it could have said 'to your maidservant likewise.' Why add 'you shall do'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי פדא. An extra word in the פסוק allows a second lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have made its point without the word תעשה. Since the Torah added it, the פסוק carries two teachings: הענקה and the comparison to the נרצע. So רבי פדא's source stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn two things from it
You shall do (the extra word that gives the second lesson)

steps.whatToRemember: From 'ואף לאמתך תעשה כן' we learn two things: a freed אמה העבריה receives הענקה, and like a נרצע she does not serve the master's son or daughter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא pattern: extra words in a פסוק allow it to teach more than one law.

steps.title: The next line of the ברייתא: the pierced slave and the one sold to a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule that a נרצע and an עבד sold to a נכרי do not serve the master's son or daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: A slave whose ear was pierced, and a Jew sold to a non-Jew, do not serve the son or the daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. This sets up the next steps, where it will look for a source for each of the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the ברייתא taught that a regular עבד עברי does serve the son after the master dies. Here are two cases that are different: the service ends with the master himself and does not pass to his children.

keyTerms.meaning: An עבד עברי whose ear was pierced because he chose to stay with his master

steps.title: Source for the pierced slave: he serves only his master
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the master pierces the slave's ear 'and he shall serve him forever', which means him and not his son or daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The pierced slave? As it is written: 'And his master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall serve him forever.' Him, but not the son or the daughter.

steps.title: What is the source for the one sold to a non-Jew?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a Jew sold to a נכרי does not serve the נכרי's heirs.

steps.title: חזקיה: 'He shall reckon with his purchaser', not with the heirs
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה learns from 'וחשב עם קנהו' that the reckoning for going free is only with the buyer himself, not with his heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: The פסוק says, 'And he shall reckon with his purchaser.' With his purchaser, and not with his purchaser's heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה gives a פסוק for the Jew sold to a נכרי. The פסוק mentions only the buyer, so the heirs are left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about counting the years left to work out the slave's redemption price. Since it says 'his purchaser', the slave owes the remaining years only to the buyer, and he goes free when the buyer dies.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall reckon with his purchaser
The heirs of his purchaser

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said:

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עם קנהו' limits the service to the buyer and leaves out his heirs.
steps.whatToRemember: Both the נרצע ('וַעֲבָדוֹ') and the one sold to a נכרי ('עִם קֹנֵהוּ') serve only the master himself, never his heirs.

steps.title: רבא: by Torah law a non-Jew inherits his father
steps.stepSummary: רבא infers from חזקיה's פסוק that a נכרי has heirs by Torah law. Otherwise the Torah would not need to exclude them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: By Torah law a non-Jew inherits his father, as it says, 'And he shall reckon with his purchaser', and not with his purchaser's heirs. This shows that he has heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא builds a new rule on חזקיה's פסוק: a נכרי inherits his father מדאורייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a נכרי had no heirs at all, there would be no reason for the Torah to say 'not with his heirs'. Since the פסוק has to leave them out, it must be that a נכרי normally does have heirs who take over his property.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
Inherits
By inference, 'from this we learn'

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule about non-Jewish inheritance: it comes from the Torah itself, not just from human custom.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.english: By Torah law a non-Jew inherits his father,
as it is stated: "And he shall reckon with his purchaser"
and not with the heirs of his purchaser.

steps.title: A convert inherits his non-Jewish father only by rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues: a גר inheriting his non-Jewish father is not Torah law, only rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: A convert inheriting the non-Jew is not from Torah law, but from the words of the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: This is still רבא speaking. He contrasts the גר with the נכרי: the גר's inheritance from his non-Jewish father exists only מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once someone becomes a גר, he is treated as a new person with no Torah-level family tie to his non-Jewish father. The Sages gave him the right to inherit anyway, but that right is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert to Judaism
From the words of the Sages, rabbinic law

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules: a נכרי inherits his father by Torah law, but a גר inherits his non-Jewish father only by rabbinic law.

phrases.english: A convert inheriting the non-Jew,
phrases.notes: He means a convert inheriting his non-Jewish father.

but from the words of the Sages.

steps.title: The משנה about a convert and a non-Jew dividing their father's estate
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that a גר may tell his non-Jewish brother to take the idols and libation wine while he takes money and produce. Once those items have come into the גר's possession, this is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: A convert and a non-Jew who inherited their non-Jewish father. The convert may say to the non-Jew, 'You take the idols and I will take money; you take the libation wine and I will take produce.' Once the items have come into the convert's possession, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove רבא's point that a גר inherits only מדרבנן. The final step of the proof comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows the גר to arrange that his brother takes the forbidden items while he takes the permitted ones. This is allowed only as long as the forbidden items have not yet come into the גר's own possession.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship, here the idols themselves
Wine poured as an offering to an idol, forbidden for benefit
Possession, domain

phrases.english: As we learned:

phrases.aramaic: גֵּר וְנׇכְרִי שֶׁיָּרְשׁוּ אֶת אֲבִיהֶם נׇכְרִי,
phrases.english: A convert and a non-Jew who inherited their father, a non-Jew,
the convert may say to the non-Jew:

phrases.aramaic: טוֹל אַתָּה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וַאֲנִי מָעוֹת,
phrases.english: You take the idols and I will take money;

phrases.aramaic: טוֹל אַתָּה יַיִן נֶסֶךְ וַאֲנִי פֵּירוֹת.
phrases.english: you take libation wine and I will take produce.
Once they have come into the convert's possession, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: גֵּר וְנׇכְרִי שֶׁיָּרְשׁוּ אֶת אֲבִיהֶם נׇכְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support רבא's claim about the גר.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that a גר inherits his non-Jewish father only מדרבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in דמאי: the גר may swap shares before the items reach his possession.

steps.title: If the inheritance were Torah law, the swap would be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: If the גר inherited by Torah law, he would own half the idols from the moment his father died. Then taking money in their place would mean taking something exchanged for idols, which is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think it is Torah law, then even when the items have not come into his possession it should be forbidden, because when he takes the money, he is taking something exchanged for idols!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה is a proof: its leniency would make no sense if the גר inherited by Torah law. The conclusion is stated in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under Torah law, a share of the inheritance would belong to the גר the moment his father died, idols included. Trading his share of the idols for money would then be benefiting from something exchanged for idols. Since the משנה permits the swap, the גר must not truly own a share by Torah law, so his inheritance is only מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it would enter your mind, 'if you think'
By Torah law
Something received in exchange for idols, also forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lets a גר swap shares before the forbidden items reach him. That proves his inheritance from a non-Jewish father is only rabbinic, just as רבא said.

phrases.english: And if you think it is Torah law,
even when they have not come into his possession, it should also be forbidden,
for when he takes, it is something exchanged for idols
that he is taking!
phrases.notes: Under Torah law he would already own half the idols, so the money he gets is payment for his share of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the משנה in step 30 proves רבא's rule.
steps.raayaObject: A גר inherits his non-Jewish father only מדרבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's permission to swap before possession would make no sense if the גר inherited by Torah law.

steps.title: So the convert's inheritance is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The proof concludes: a גר inherits his non-Jewish father only מדרבנן, a decree so he will not go back to his old ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is by rabbinic law. It is a decree the Rabbis made, so that he will not return to his old ways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof from the last step. Since the swap of idols for money is allowed, the גר must not really own the idols by Torah law, so his inheritance must be only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גר inherited מדאורייתא, half the idols would be his and swapping them for money would be forbidden. Since the משנה allows it, his inheritance must be only a rabbinic decree. The reason for the decree: if he lost his inheritance by converting, he might go back to being a non-Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not by Torah law
A protective decree made by the Rabbis
Lest he return to his old (non-Jewish) ways

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why a גר does receive his father's estate in practice, even though the Torah itself does not give it to him.

phrases.english: Rather: it is by rabbinic law,
it is a decree that the Rabbis made
lest he return to his old ways.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof built in steps 30-31.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A גר inherits his non-Jewish father only מדרבנן, as a decree to keep him from returning to his old ways.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this: inheritance yes, partnership no
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the idol-swap is allowed only when they inherited, but forbidden when the גר and the non-Jew were partners.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: In what case is this said? When they inherited. But when they formed a partnership, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבא's conclusion. The swap is allowed for an inheritance but not for a partnership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a partnership the גר truly owns half of everything, idols included, so getting money in their place is getting something exchanged for idols. With inheritance the swap is allowed, which shows that by Torah law the גר never owned the idols. The difference between the two cases supports the idea that his inheritance is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the point)
In what case are these words said? (limits a rule)
They became partners

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: "These words" means the permission to let the non-Jewish brother take the idols while the גר takes money.

phrases.english: When they inherited,
but when they formed a partnership – it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the conclusion of step 32 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a גר's inheritance from his non-Jewish father is only rabbinic.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that limits the idol-swap permission to inheritance, not partnership.

steps.title: No inheritance from a convert, not even rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: A נכרי inheriting a גר, and a גר inheriting a גר, has no basis in Torah law or in rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-Jew inheriting a convert, and a convert inheriting a convert, is not by Torah law and not by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list of inheritance cases. Here it moves to cases where the one who died is the גר himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, a son who became a גר still inherits his non-Jewish father מדרבנן. Here the father is the גר. His non-Jewish son does not inherit him, and neither does his son who also converted, not even מדרבנן. This is because conversion cuts the family tie, and there is no reason for a rabbinic decree here.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert to Judaism
A non-Jew
From the words of the scribes, meaning rabbinic law

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the direction. Step 32 was a גר inheriting his non-Jewish father, which works מדרבנן. Here the one who died is the גר, and nobody inherits him at all.

phrases.english: A non-Jew [inheriting] a convert,
and a convert [inheriting] a convert –
is not by Torah law
and not by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: נׇכְרִי אֶת הַגֵּר, וְגֵר אֶת הַגֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the case of a גר inheriting a non-Jew, it adds the cases where a גר is the one being inherited.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither a non-Jew nor a fellow convert inherits a convert, by Torah law or by rabbinic law.

steps.title: Proof from the loan owed to a convert
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that if someone borrowed from a גר whose sons converted with him, he does not repay the sons, and the Sages are not pleased if he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One who borrowed money from a convert whose sons converted with him should not return it to his sons. And if he did return it, the Sages are not pleased with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the last rule from a משנה. The sons of a גר do not inherit a debt owed to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sons inherited even מדרבנן, the borrower would have to repay them. The משנה says he does not repay them, and the Sages even disapprove if he does. This shows there is no inheritance at all, not even rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: He borrowed money
The Sages are not pleased with him

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
One who borrowed money from a convert
phrases.notes: The case is that the convert who lent the money has died. The question is who gets paid back.

phrases.english: whose sons converted with him –
he does not return it to his sons.
And if he did return it –
the spirit of the Sages is not pleased with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the rule stated in step 34.
steps.raayaObject: That a גר's sons do not inherit him, even מדרבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a loan from a גר whose sons converted with him.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the Sages are pleased
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the Sages are pleased with one who repays the sons, which contradicts the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא that the Sages are pleased with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. A ברייתא says the opposite of the משנה it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the Sages are not pleased when the borrower repays the sons. The ברייתא says they are pleased. Both cannot be right about the same case, so the גמרא needs to explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages are pleased with him

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא
the spirit of the Sages is pleased with him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה brought as proof in step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the Sages are not pleased with one who repays the sons.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the Sages are pleased with him, which directly contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: Different cases: a son conceived and born before conversion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer: the משנה speaks of a son who was both conceived and born before the family converted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, it speaks of a son whose conception and birth were not in holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the contradiction by saying the two sources speak about different sons. This amud covers only the first case; the second case comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (Sages not pleased) speaks of a son who was conceived and born while his father was still a non-Jew. That son has no family tie to his father at all, so repaying him is not what the Sages want. The ברייתא (Sages pleased) must speak of a different kind of son, which the גמרא explains next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
His conception and his birth
Not in holiness, meaning not as a Jew

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, where his conception and his birth
were not in holiness,
phrases.notes: "Not in holiness" means both happened before the family converted, while they were not yet Jewish.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן שֶׁהוֹרָתוֹ וְלֵידָתוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the contradiction raised in step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source speaks about a different son.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seemed to speak about the same son and to disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of a son both conceived and born before conversion. The ברייתא's case is explained next.
